newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ITALY PREPARE TO TAKE OVER AT THE TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALY PREPARE TO TAKE OVER AT THE TOP.

text.p: Gianfranco Zola's lone strike for Italy against England at Wembley last month means that a win over Moldova in Trieste on Saturday will lift the 1994 losing finalists to the top of their World Cup qualifying group.
For the Italians, it is the start of an important month as they go on to face Poland home and away in April and three wins out of three would virtually seal their qualification as group winners.
Coach Cesare Maldini is likely to stick as closely as he can to the side which won 1-0 against England but he already has one enforced change to consider.
In the absence through injury of Pier Luigi Casiraghi and Fabrizio Ravanelli, he looks certain to give the 23-year-old Juventus forward Christian Vieri his first cap as Zola's striking partner.

"Vieri is the player who physically most resembles the two absentees...and if you want to say that Vieri will be playing, then say it", said Maldini who knows enough about his man after capping him 19 times at Under 21 level.
With Moldova having lost all three qualifiers so far, the signs are good for the Italians.
Their game, however, is just one of nine qualifying matches being played in Europe on Saturday, several of which will have a significant bearing on who gets to France next year.
In group one, the two favourites, Croatia and Denmark, meet in Split in a replay of their Euro '96 match which the Croatians won 3-0.
However, the early running in the group has been made by Greece and the Croatians, in particular, know that any points dropped on Saturday could prove crucial in the run-in.

"This game is our 'to be or not to be'," said Croatian coach Miroslav Blazevic who has called up two newcomers in the shape of defender Niko Kovac of German first division Bayer Leverkusen and midfielder Nenad Pralija of Spain's Espanyol
The Danes, who have won both of their early games, will be without their captain Michael Laudrup who has cited a lack of training as his excuse for dropping out.
In Kilmarnock, Scotland have the chance to exorcise some old ghosts when they host Estonia in group four.

The fiasco in Tallinn in October when the Estonians failed to turn up led to that match being replayed last month and, rather than producing the expected Scottish landslide, ended in an embarrasing 0-0 draw.
The Scots lead their group with eight points from four games but, with another match against second-placed Austria on Wednesday, Craig Brown's men need all the points to maintain their momentum.

In group seven, the high-flying Dutch should have no problems against San Marino but the other match pits second-placed Wales against Belgium, who are one point behind them with two games in hand. Defeat for Wales would signal the end of their World Cup hopes.
There are also two games in group nine. Leaders Portugal travel to Belfast to play Northern Ireland while Albania's match against Ukraine has been moved to Granada in Spain for security reasons.

Portuguese coach Artur Jorge, physically attacked on Wednesday by Sporting Lisbon striker Ricardo Sa Pinto after dropping him, has called up veteran Porto midfielder Rui Barros in place of the injured Pedro Barbosa.
Russia currently top group five on goal difference but with rivals Israel playing Luxembourg on Sunday, they will be keen to register a high goal tally against Cyprus in Nicosia on Saturday.

The Russians will be without striker Anatoly Kanishchev and midfielder Yevgeny Kharlachev but victory should be a formality against a Cyprus team which is lacking seven regulars, has a new coach and is still being rocked by allegations of throwing their last match against Bulgaria.
Group eight leaders Romania have the opportunity to improve their goal difference as they host a Liechtenstein defence which has leaked 21 goals in four games.
